name: Mega Flex Plastics Limited
summary:
Mega Flex is a regional producer of agricultural leno bags and woven packaging. It also sources fabric from a related supplier and has a small PLC-hardware trading business. FY2026 brought a genuine recovery in bag volumes and operating margins. Substantial liquid mutual funds support ordinary expansion, even after excluding earmarked cash and disputed tax recoverables.

However, ₹157.40 prices in much more than ordinary recovery. The five-year model produces approximately −11.8% annualized return in the base case and +8.5% in a strong, funded bull case. Treat this as a cyclical/recovery business with mixed capital allocation, not an established compounder. A new purchase also remains on Hold because complete trading liquidity is unverified. Better capacity evidence, sustained conversion margins, controlled related-party exposure and a materially lower price could change the conclusion. A lower price alone would not solve the lot-size and exit problem.
classification: Not actionable: valuation unattractive; tradability Hold—unresolved. Mixed-quality cyclical/recovery, not a compounder.

IAS.override: IAS NS because L is missing and G4 implementation remains on Hold.

GOV.rationale: Related-supplier lending, procurement and rent create minority-allocation conflicts; repayment schedules are not stipulated. Unmodified audit, disclosed loan rate, no reported overdue loan and nil March promoter pledge are substantial positives. Conditional monitoring, not an evidenced integrity failure.

MOAT.rationale: Commodity packaging is contestable. Brands, quality and local distribution support service, but no verified persistent pricing premium, switching cost, dominant share or durable excess return establishes a stronger moat.

REV.rationale: Preselected FY2023–FY2026 manufactured-revenue CAGR is approximately12%, corroborated by10.65% physical bag growth. Band6, net adjustment0. The five-year nominal series is distorted by pandemic base and new PLC trading.

DUR.rationale: Repeat agriculture and cold-storage demand provides access. Current concentration, contracts and installed utilization are unavailable. Forecast volume requires actual capacity or procurement expansion; the market size alone does not establish duration.

CAP.rationale: Matched FY2023–FY2025 incremental return including supplier interest and net rent is12.72%, below the13–17% capital-cost test. FY2026 recovery is positive contrary evidence. Negative three-year capital increment is NM; the five-year121.8% accounting proxy is not project ROI.

CASH.rationale: Reported FY2023–FY2026 CFO/PAT is48.46%. Removing related-loan balance movement gives a classification sensitivity, not proven cash conversion because accrued interest is included. FY2026 cash recovery and low receivables are positives, but advance releases and payables growth are not indefinitely repeatable.

BAL.rationale: Liquid funds materially exceed debt and ordinary modeled uses after conservative restrictions and asset haircuts. Not a9: current redemption quality, supplier-loan exposure, disputed tax assets, guarantees and allocation remain relevant risks.

EXEC.rationale: Commissioned looms/Nova machines and operating solar are supported by annual reports and the August AGM. Volume recovered. Land funding remains unspent in the last verified report; project-level returns, current utilization and metered savings remain unverified.

EARN.rationale: FY2026 profit and operating EBITDA show a genuine rebound. Margins were highly variable and other income remains significant. Mid-cycle6.5% EBITDA margin is used rather than assuming the latest seasonal peak persists.

R.rationale: Base five-year annualized return is−11.81%, about26.81 percentage points below the15% hurdle: rubric minimum1. The strong funded bull remains below the hurdle. Unfunded stresses have ordinary returns NS.

D.rationale: The funded bear implies about85.6% terminal price downside even without insolvency. Asset recovery, margin compression, customer loss and poor liquidity can combine. Cash-rich corporate solvency does not protect against entry-price overpayment.

P.rationale: Base15% hurdle entry is approximately₹41.75 versus₹157.40. Even the strong bull gives approximately₹117.62. Base growth requires40.29x terminal EBITDA to earn15%; the quote offers no modeled margin of safety.

L.rationale: Only12 of20 and33 of60 issuer observations are present. Missing rows are unknown, not zero. Full-window liquidity and spreads are NS. Observed medians do not permit a whole1,000-share lot at2%,5% or10% participation.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Mega Flex is a regional producer of agricultural leno bags and woven packaging. It also sources fabric from a related supplier and has a small PLC-hardware trading business. FY2026 brought a genuine recovery in bag volumes and operating margins. Substantial liquid mutual funds support ordinary expansion, even after excluding earmarked cash and disputed tax recoverables.

However, ₹157.40 prices in much more than ordinary recovery. The five-year model produces approximately −11.8% annualized return in the base case and +8.5% in a strong, funded bull case. Treat this as a cyclical/recovery business with mixed capital allocation, not an established compounder. A new purchase also remains on Hold because complete trading liquidity is unverified. Better capacity evidence, sustained conversion margins, controlled related-party exposure and a materially lower price could change the conclusion. A lower price alone would not solve the lot-size and exit problem.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff: 20 October 2026. Legal entity: Mega Flex Plastics Limited; CIN L25209WB2003PLC097273; ISIN INE0G1D01014; NSE Emerge symbol MEGAFLEX, series SM. The accounts are standalone Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, with no subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures. Latest audited year: 31 March 2026. September 2026 half-year results were not available by the cutoff.

The latest actual trade was 19 October 2026 at ₹157.40. The cutoff fell on an exchange holiday, so no synthetic 20 October quote is used. Issued shares are 12,131,025 and market capitalization is ₹190.94cr. The current lot is 1,000 shares, not the old IPO lot of 3,000. Horizon: 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031; nominal pre-tax equity hurdle: 15%; reference position: ₹500,000.

Confidence is high on audited financial statements, identity and current share count; medium on organic growth, sustainable margins and incremental economics; low on complete execution liquidity. G1 integrity, G2 reliability and G3 funding are Conditional, not failed. G4 is Hold—unresolved for new-purchase implementation. An unmodified audit is not a guarantee, but neither a price clarification nor missing private information establishes fraud, manipulation or default. Business and growth quality remain comparable; investment ranking does not.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS is 4.84, displayed as 4.8. GQS is 5.25, displayed as 5.3. Both have 100% factor coverage. IAS is NS: the known contribution is 2.06 with 90% coverage, and the missing-L bounds are 2.16–3.06. These bounds are not a point estimate or probability distribution. No governance, funding or growth-quality numeric override is triggered.

The canonical factor scores are GOV5, MOAT3, REV6, DUR5, CAP4, CASH5, BAL8, EXEC5, EARN5, R1, D2, P1 and LNS. Exact weights and contributions are retained below and in the canonical record. Unrounded BQS feeds IAS, and display rounding is conventional half-up.

Controlled overlap matters: physical and economic growth informs REV, durable demand access informs DUR, capital productivity informs CAP, and actual cash realization informs CASH. Brands, TAM, an order pipeline or a high latest-year ROCE receive no extra, unlisted bonus. The factor register records both supporting and contrary evidence. In particular, the FY2026 recovery is not erased by earlier weak economics, while one strong year does not establish a moat or repeatable incremental returns.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Polypropylene granules are extruded into tapes, woven into leno fabric, then cut and stitched into produce bags. The company also supplies woven fabric and sutli. Agriculture, cold storage and other packaging requirements drive demand. Brands, product quality and the West Bengal delivery network help customer access, but revenue comes from shipment of goods, not subscriptions or protected concessions. Revenue excludes indirect taxes and discounts.

FY2026 finished-goods sales of ₹74.0588cr plus traded-goods sales of ₹4.0168cr reconcile to ₹78.0756cr operating revenue. Trading was 5.14% of sales. Note22 explicitly identifies traded purchases of ₹3.5434cr as PLC Hardware, versus ₹1.7159cr in FY2025. The trading spread before other expenses was ₹0.4734cr, or 11.79%, not a software margin. References elsewhere to granule trading, industrial automation or future diversification do not establish that these are the principal profit engine.

Manufacturing raw materials include granules, yarn, tape and fabric. Related supplier White Saffron Grains LLP supplied ₹36.9685cr including GST and also received a ₹8.1827cr loan. Finished-goods accounting therefore does not prove wholly in-house value addition. Conversely, manufacturing labor, electricity, inventory and plant assets establish real conversion activity. Exact own-production versus outsourced economics are not disclosed. Supplier advances of ₹4.4326cr matter more to funding than the small ₹0.4198cr receivable balance.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Service proximity, reliable bag quality, repeat relationships and local delivery can reduce fulfillment friction. They are narrower advantages than scarce intellectual property, contractual switching costs or durable pricing power. Polymer prices and competing packaging suppliers constrain pricing. The IPO prospectus disclosed FY2022 top-ten customer concentration of 79.21%, top-five concentration of 67.11% and top-ten supplier concentration of 97.88%. These are historical risk indicators, not verified current concentration figures.

Rishi Techtex's FY2025 primary woven-division discussion describes price-sensitive industrial sacks and limited differentiation. It is a useful economic comparator, but its industrial and agrotech mix is not identical. No unverified current peer multiple is imported into this valuation.

Mega Flex's brands and 83.7 million bags sold establish operating scale, not market share or superior returns. Buyer concentration, delayed commodity pass-through, substitution and reliance on procured fabric can erase a year's margin improvement. MOAT3 reflects the absence of demonstrated durable competitive advantage, not a claim that every customer buys solely on price. Current customer retention, share gains, repeat order quality and price premiums remain open questions.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The five-year reported revenue CAGR from FY2021 to FY2026 is about 21.5%, but its start is a pandemic trough and its end includes a new PLC trading activity. The preselected REV anchor is therefore FY2023–FY2026 constant-scope manufactured revenue: ₹52.6855cr to ₹74.0588cr, approximately 12.0% CAGR. Physical bag sales increased from 61.79 million to 83.70 million, approximately 10.65% CAGR. This supports the 10–15% band, REV6, with no adjustment.

No acquisition was identified. Manufacturing sales growth includes physical volume, polymer-price pass-through, mix and sales of fabric/sutli. Dividing all manufacturing revenue by bag units gives only a mixed-product realization proxy, not a clean average bag price. In FY2025 manufactured sales rose 20.47% while bags sold fell 0.88%. In FY2026 manufactured sales rose 27.00% while bag volume increased 20.17%. The latest rebound is not merely price inflation, but the five-year nominal CAGR is not a clean physical growth rate either.

The historical table retains annual rupee additions, manufacturing/trading splits and available volume data. FY2020–FY2022 production quantities are not silently substituted for later bags sold. A precise five-year constant-price organic series remains unavailable; the available three-year triangulation is sufficient for a medium-confidence REV score, not for a high-growth premium.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Repeat agricultural and cold-storage consumption provides accessible demand, and FY2026 sales growth is actual evidence rather than a large-TAM claim. Growth still requires capacity, fabric procurement or job-work arrangements, distribution and working capital.

The prospectus disclosed FY2022 annual bag capacity of 51.307 million and production of 46.498 million, or 90.63% utilization. That old denominator cannot be divided into 83.7 million current bags sold. Subsequent machines, product mix and purchased fabric have changed. A valid FY2026 utilization rate cannot be reconstructed.

Four wide-width looms were described as adding 419 MT of fabric capacity; two Nova machines together added 1.71 million bags. Their ₹1.0602cr commissioning supports some growth, but does not establish capacity for the model's FY2032 base volume of 132.82 million bags or bull volume of 193.60 million. Those are required operating paths, not claimed installed capacity. Forecasts charge maintenance capex of 1.8% of sales and growth capex at four times incremental sales/capital, plus operating working capital. No growth revenue is credited to unspent Odisha land funding.

Aligned FY2023–FY2025 incremental NOPAT/capital was 12.72%, below the 13–17% capital-cost test. FY2026's rebound is important contrary evidence. GQS5.25 reflects real physical growth with incomplete proof of durable margins, capacity scaling and attributable incremental returns.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Longstanding executive leadership offers operating continuity. Primary shareholding at 31 March 2026 shows promoters and their group holding 73.92%, public holders 26.08%, 1,026,000 promoter shares locked in, and no promoter pledge or outstanding warrants/ESOPs. These are March observations, not a claim about October unlocked float. The narrower annual-report list of four named promoters is not the full promoter group. The 19 October security master independently verifies current issued capital.

The ₹8.1827cr related-supplier loan carries a stated 9% rate. CARO says principal and interest repayment schedules were not stipulated, so the auditor could not assess regularity. It also reports no overdue amount and terms not prejudicial, based on information supplied. This is a contractual-control and capital-allocation concern, not proof of an uncollectible loan. Related-party figures labelled interest received do not by themselves establish cash collection: FY2024's loan movement includes an interest accrual. The ₹36.9685cr procurement figure includes GST and must not be divided by tax-exclusive expenses as an exact concentration ratio.

Full FY2026 opinion, CARO, IFC and audit-trail reports were read. The opinion is unmodified; controls are reported adequate and effective; the audit trail operated and was preserved without observed tampering; quarterly bank returns agreed. No default, wilful default, fraud or whistleblower complaint was reported. Secretarial compliance has a narrower scope and is not a tax audit. Auditor rotation is not inferred to be a resignation. The October price clarification is not evidence of manipulation; the 2016 CRISIL non-cooperation suspension is not a current default.

Loom/Nova commissioning and operation of the 400 kW solar facility are supported by annual reports and the August AGM. Solar began in March 2025, not newly in FY2026. Metered savings and project-level returns remain unavailable. The ₹4.3694cr Odisha land allocation was still unspent in the last audited use-of-proceeds statement. This distinguishes commissioning evidence from economic delivery.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Operating EBITDA is defined consistently as PBT plus finance cost, less all other income, plus depreciation. FY2026 operating EBITDA is ₹8.069cr, not a larger number including treasury income. PAT of ₹7.2727cr less 75% of other income of ₹2.5634cr gives an illustrative normalized PAT of ₹5.35015cr; actual tax composition may differ. Excluding all other income also excludes supplier interest and rent, so it is a conservative core-earnings proxy. FY2024 had negative core EBIT despite positive reported PAT.

FY2026 CFO of ₹17.622cr consists of ₹8.8000cr pre-working-capital cash, approximately ₹11.1973cr working-capital/provision movements, less ₹2.3753cr tax. Significant releases included ₹3.8237cr of short-term advances and ₹3.9606cr of additional payables. Supplier advances fell from ₹9.0837cr to ₹4.4326cr. This cash recovery is real in the audited statement, but cannot recur at the same rate indefinitely.

FY2023–FY2026 reported CFO was ₹6.8891cr versus PAT of ₹14.2170cr, or 48.46%. Adding back ₹6.2475cr of related-loan balance movement produces a classification sensitivity of ₹13.1366cr, not demonstrated cash conversion of 92.4%. FY2024's loan balance reconciles as 674.18 + 176.50 − 95.61 + 72.40 = 827.47 lakh: the movement includes accrued interest. A cash disbursement/collection bridge is needed before treating the adjustment as cash. The separate non-related FY2022 advance also prevents equating total loan growth with related-loan growth.

Committed operating/supply-chain capital equals equity plus debt, less cash, financial investments and the ₹6.5738093cr disputed GST deposit. Supplier-loan capital and rent-generating PPE remain included. The matched FY2023–FY2025 numerator therefore adds known after-tax supplier interest and net rental income: ₹1.2254cr additional NOPAT divided by ₹9.6347cr additional capital gives 12.72%. Three-year negative capital increments are NM, not infinite returns. The five-year 121.8% ex-other-income accounting proxy is dominated by margin and working-capital reversal, not proven project ROI. The supplier loan's approximate after-tax book yield is 6.62%, before credit loss or unmeasured strategic benefits.

Gratuity of ₹0.6639cr is not actuarially measured. Quoted investments cost ₹3.9467cr against market value ₹3.5537cr; liquid funds cost ₹28.6795cr against market value ₹29.2568cr. The model uses fund cost and quoted market value, with separate haircuts and no value for unquoted holdings/silver. FY2025 EPS presentation has an unresolved weighted-average versus end-share reconciliation; economic end-share EPS avoids overstating forward earnings. FY2025 warrant conversion raised ₹5.544cr and expanded shares 12.90%, diluting prior ownership 11.43%. There is no assumed remaining warrant dilution.

FY2022 CFO differs between the prospectus and the later audited comparison despite identical ending cash; classification comparability is flagged, not labelled fraud. FY2021 gross capex is ND, not negative capex inferred from net asset disposals.

The cash map starts with ₹4.9849cr reported cash, subtracts ₹0.5145cr lien deposits and ₹4.4070cr warrant earmark, leaving ₹0.0634cr free cash, plus ₹28.6795cr liquid funds. Earmark/lien overlap is unverified; subtracting both is conservative. The model settles debt, net tax, statutory dues, book gratuity and detailed unpaid minor tax claims before receipts. Supplier payables enter working capital once. No undrawn facility is assumed.

The major ₹6.5738093cr GST amount was already paid under protest. It is valued at zero, not charged again as fresh cash. Detailed minor CARO claims net of deposits total ₹0.0537088cr, about ₹45,088 above the rounded note30 implication. The older ₹0.4610796cr entry-tax claim disappears from FY2026; a September 2025 Supreme Court withdrawal to seek settlement does not prove payment. A ₹1.0763cr bank guarantee is not automatically an extra cash loss; a distinct call stress net of lien security is ₹0.5618cr, only if it does not duplicate an underlying obligation.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
A mid-cycle operating EV/EBITDA model is preferable to headline P/E that capitalizes treasury income while ignoring the financial assets generating it. At ₹157.40, market capitalization is ₹190.94cr, FY2026 P/E is 26.25x and normalized ex-other-income PAT P/E is approximately 35.69x. Liquid-fund/free-cash-adjusted EV is approximately ₹164.15cr before separate quoted stakes and supplier-loan recovery, or 20.34x operating EBITDA.

Base assumptions are 8% manufacturing volume growth, 2% price/mix, 8% trading growth, 6.5% EBITDA margin, working capital at 18% of sales and 9x terminal EBITDA. Bear begins with a 15% volume contraction and 4% price decline, then 3% volume growth, with 3.5% margin and 6x multiple. Bull assumes 15% volume growth, 2% price/mix, 12% trading growth, a sustained 10.5% margin and 12x multiple. The bull is intentionally strong relative to the latest 10.34% margin, not a disguised base case.

All cases charge 1.8% maintenance capex, growth capex at incremental sales divided by four, 25% operating cash tax and a ₹3cr retained reserve. Supplier-loan recoveries are 0/50/100%, quoted-equity haircuts 40/10/0%, and land recoveries 50/80/100%. No treasury yield, loan interest or investment dividend is forecast. Warrant cash funds only the designated land/GCP use, without free incremental earnings. Ordinary bear, base and bull remain funded without new debt or equity.

The March balance sheet is rolled forward to the October entry date, then through each March year-end and the October 2031 exit. October cash is modeled, not observed. Each interval conservatively prefunds reinvestment and old claims before operating receipts. Any cash-floor breach, including pre-entry, suppresses ordinary returns and hurdle-entry prices. Rescue is separately labelled, with whole shares, issue discount, fees and dilution.

Terminal EBITDA is the FY2032 forward annualized run-rate, approximately five months forward of the exit date, not additional cash earned before exit. Terminal EV plus excess cash and haircut non-operating assets, less debt, is divided by diluted shares. The retained reserve is not excess cash. No dividends are double counted.

Five-year annualized returns are approximately −32.1% bear, −11.8% base and +8.5% bull. Base hurdle entries at 12/15/18% are approximately ₹47.65/₹41.75/₹36.71. These are conditional model values, not executable recommendations. At base growth and margins, the quoted price requires 40.29x terminal EBITDA to deliver 15%. There is no finite funded volume-growth crossing within the tested −5% to 60% range: high growth absorbs funding before meeting the return requirement. An infeasible endpoint is not reported as a solution. All annual paths and sensitivity grids are embedded, including infeasible rows.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that recent volume growth, wide-width products and solar savings sustain double-digit margins while liquid funds finance capacity. The funded bull explicitly tests 15% volume growth and a 10.5% margin, yet yields only 8.5%, below the 15% hurdle. An unattractive valuation therefore does not depend on alleging fraud or imminent insolvency.

Permanent loss can arise from paying a high multiple for peak conversion profits, then waiting through poor liquidity as margins normalize, customers switch, advances rebuild and related assets recover poorly. The funded bear ends near ₹22.68 per share, about 85.6% below entry before trading costs. A 20% customer-volume-loss sensitivity is illustrative because current concentration is ND, not a prediction about a named customer.

A 10% polymer-input shock, roughly 70% material exposure and a quarter-year pass-through delay imply about 1.75 percentage points of margin pressure. The persistent-lag stress also raises working capital and haircuts liquid funds; it breaches the reserve later, so ordinary return is NS. Contractual escalation terms and actual lag are not disclosed.

The linked severe case combines 1% EBITDA margin, working capital at 45% of sales, ₹12cr extra capex, volume/price weakness and asset haircuts. Its unfunded ordinary return is suppressed. A separate hypothetical recap finances each gap through whole-share issuance and reports fees, dilution and the original holder's negative return. This is not a forecast of approved fundraising. A verified liquid-asset shortfall, sustained negative conversion margins or unexplained related-party transfers would break the thesis faster than a small EPS presentation discrepancy.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
At ₹157.40, five times the share price is ₹787 and ten times is ₹1,574, before dividends and dilution. Required five-year annualized price growth is approximately 37.97% and 58.49%. At unchanged shares, the corresponding equity values are ₹954.71cr and ₹1,909.42cr.

At 12x EBITDA and 9% EBITDA margin, ignoring non-operating assets for this illustrative hurdle, revenues would need to be approximately ₹884cr and ₹1,768cr. That is more than eleven and twenty-two times FY2026 revenue. The associated plant, procurement, working capital and possible dilution make the task harder, not easier. These are arithmetic requirements, not forecasts inferred from a broad market size.

Even the funded bull reaches only approximately ₹200.84cr forward FY2032 revenue and 193.60 million bags. The evidence does not support a five-times or ten-times wealth thesis from the quoted entry, and no multibagger or proven-compounder designation is warranted.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Track physical bags sold against the FY2026 baseline of 83.7 million, separating manufactured sales, PLC trading and price/mix. Two seasonal half-years of falling volume, or a full-year operating margin below 4%, would undermine the growth case. Monitor supplier advances of ₹4.4326cr and payables of ₹4.1367cr; an unwind of more than ₹3cr without replacement liquidity warrants a fresh funding model.

Monitor the ₹8.1827cr related loan, accrued versus collected interest, repayment terms and independent procurement pricing. Growth in the balance without measurable strategic benefit weakens capital allocation. Verify liquid-fund redemption quality and current free cash against dated uses plus the ₹3cr reserve.

Require a physical capacity/procurement bridge before underwriting 132.82 million base or 193.60 million bull bags. Obtain metered solar savings, capital-cohort profit and Odisha land milestones. Follow the GST appeal number/status, the separate entry-tax settlement, actuarial gratuity and any new guarantee call without duplicating paid claims.

Refresh the audit opinion, CARO, controls, bank-return reconciliation and minority protections. For implementation, require complete primary 20/60-session activity, including genuine zero-trade observations, current lot size, restrictions, spread and executable bid depth. September 2026 half-year results are the next financial checkpoint; compare like-for-like seasonal periods rather than annualizing H1 against a stronger H2. This monitoring plan does not place orders or authorize automatic trades.

Without assigning zeros to missing rows, an additional bound is available: even if all27 missing sessions had arbitrarily high turnover, the60-session median could not exceed₹391,700. At5% participation, a₹500,000 exit would require at least25.53 fractional days. One current lot costs₹157,400, exceeding even10% of that optimistic median bound. This strengthens the implementation caution without pretending to know the true median.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Business quality of 4.84 and growth quality of 5.25 are fully scoreable, mixed rather than compounder grade. IAS is NS because liquidity is not scoreable and G4 remains on Hold. Its 2.16–3.06 missing-data bounds would all fall in the weak-setup range, but bounds are not a scored investment classification.

Action category: not actionable for a new purchase; valuation unattractive at ₹157.40 even before the trading hold. There is no governance-Avoid override and no assumed ordinary-case funding failure. A price near the base 15% hurdle entry of ₹41.75 would satisfy this particular model, not establish certain fair value or executable liquidity.

Better physical growth, verified capacity, capital returns and cash could justify a different valuation. A lower price without liquidity and related-party clarity is not enough. Existing holders need their actual position size, tax context and available bids considered separately; a quoted mark is not necessarily a realizable exit. This is business/security research, not an executed trade or personalized allocation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources control identity, financial statements, issued shares and the quote. Four complete annual reports, IPO restated accounts, May 2026 results, the August AGM and March shareholding were inspected. The canonical record includes source URLs, document hashes, page locators, extracted financial rows and complete model assumptions/results.

The Calcutta High Court text is a judicial-text mirror, clearly labelled. Its adverse May 2026 GST classification ruling and the annual report's intended Supreme Court appeal are distinct from the September 2025 Supreme Court entry-tax withdrawal. The specific May20 issuer litigation update and a later primary GST SLP/stay were searched for but not directly retrieved. Absence of retrieval does not establish that no appeal exists. Secondary coverage reverses part of the historical classification description, so it does not control the facts.

Open questions are current owned/outsourced capacity and utilization; customer concentration and price-escalation contracts; net-of-GST related procurement and independent pricing; loan cash collections and repayment schedule; liquid-fund holdings, redemption and cash restrictions; actuarial gratuity; GST appeal and entry-tax settlement evidence; project economics and land timing; EPS/predeposit reconciliation; and complete trading activity and restrictions.

Model assumptions are explicit, not replacements for missing observations. All ordinary and rescue paths enforce cash-floor guards. Source-safe backups contain analyst-created extracts, calculations and source identifiers, not source PDFs, full OCR, personal tax identifiers or individual shareholder lists. Independent model/source review and verified archive reconstruction precede final batch acceptance.
